newsitem.title: OMAN: Japan-Oman trade grows 2.6 percent in 1996.
newsitem.headline: Japan-Oman trade grows 2.6 percent in 1996.

text.p: Trade between Japan and Oman rose 2.6 percent in dollar terms last year to $2.61 billion, the Japan External Trade Organisation (JETRO) said on Sunday.
But in yen terms, bilateral trade -- mostly in oil, electronics, machinery, transport equipment, metal products, rubber products and textiles -- shot up 18.3 percent.
Japanese exports to Oman showed a slight decline to $657.2 million in 1996 from $684.4 million in 1995, but in yen terms Japanese exports grew 10.2 percent, JETRO said.

"Now the yen, being depreciated a little against the U.S. dollar and the competitiveness of the Japanese products having increased, exports are expected to increase in volume and in value during the current year," it said in a statement.
JETRO said almost 10 percent more cars, or a total 14,322, were exported to Oman in the year.
Japanese imports from Oman -- mostly crude oil -- rose five percent in dollar terms, or 21.2 percent in yen terms, to $1.96 billion. Crude accounted for 94.2 percent of total imports.
